The service targets staffing agencies, enterprises, and hiring teams, providing tools for interview coordination, candidate engagement, and analytics. Backed by Radical Ventures, Ribbon AI aims to streamline hiring processes and improve recruitment efficiency.

providers.name: VNLIFE
providers.description: VNLIFE is the Vietnamese technology and financial-services holding group whose flagship business is VNPAY (Vietnam Payment Solution Joint Stock Company), the leading electronic-payment provider in Vietnam. VNLIFE operates a payments and lifestyle ecosystem spanning the VNPAY-QR payment gateway (integrated across 40+ banks and 15+ e-wallets), SmartPOS/PhonePOS acceptance hardware, the VNPAY super-app, VnShop e-commerce, taxi booking, e-invoicing, and B2B payment platforms serving 350,000+ merchants, 450,000+ acceptance points, and 60M+ users. The VNPAY payment gateway is exposed as a documented redirect/IPN HTTP API (VNPAY-QR / vpcpay) secured with HMAC-SHA512 checksums. VNLIFE is backed by investors including SoftBank Vision Fund and GIC.

providers.name: Copper Banking
providers.description: Copper (Copper Banking) is a Seattle-based consumer fintech founded in 2019 by Eddie Behringer and Stefan Berglund that began as a teen banking app and debit card built on the Synapse banking-as-a-service platform. After Synapse's collapse Copper abruptly discontinued its bank deposit accounts and debit cards in May 2024 and repositioned as a financial-empowerment and earning app, where members earn cash and gift-card rewards through cash back, surveys, receipt scanning, games and referrals, alongside financial-literacy content, guides and in-school workshops. Copper publishes no public developer portal, documentation or API specification; the only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is an OAuth 2.0 authorization server for a Model Context Protocol endpoint at mcp.getcopper.com.

providers.name: LendInvest
providers.description: LendInvest is a London-based fintech property finance platform and mortgage lender, founded in 2013 after spinning out of Montello Bridging Finance, and listed on the London Stock Exchange AIM market under the ticker LINV since July 2021. It originates and services short-term bridging finance, property development finance, buy-to-let and residential mortgages for UK intermediaries, brokers, property developers, landlords and investors, and runs a parallel capital business that lets individual, corporate and institutional investors put money into secured UK property loans. The company distributes almost entirely through mortgage intermediaries via its Mortgages Portal, and was the first UK fintech to securitise its own buy-to-let loan book. LendInvest publishes no public developer API, developer portal or SDKs; its broker and borrower integrations run through hosted portals rather than a documented public API surface.

providers.name: 8B Education Investments
providers.description: 8B Education Investments (legally 8B Finance, Inc., trading as 8B) is a New York headquartered education-finance company founded in 2017 by Lydiah Kemunto Bosire that helps African students pay for degrees at universities outside Africa. It operates a student-loan marketplace and eligibility comparison tool, an income-share and guarantee backed lending program originated with partner banks including Nelnet Bank, a University Reserve admissions product, and a free community platform of prospective and current students offering scholarships, courses, forums, events and job listings. 8B publishes no public developer program or API reference; the only machine-readable surfaces it serves are an llms.txt on its marketing site and an OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol endpoint exposed by its WordPress stack.

providers.name: Sardine
providers.description: Sardine is a San Francisco-based fraud prevention, AML compliance, and risk management platform for fintechs, banks, marketplaces, and crypto VASPs. It unifies onboarding (KYC, KYB, document and bank verification), device intelligence and behavioral biometrics, payment and card fraud scoring, AML transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and case management into a single risk operating system. Sardine's "agentic" layer applies atomic agents (OSINT, data analysis, transaction monitoring, business due diligence, sanctions screening) to compress investigation time from days to minutes, while Sonar provides cross-industry fraud intelligence across the consortium. The platform serves 400+ enterprise customers including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Nubank, Novo, and bunq, has screened $1.3T+ in payments, and profiled 5.4B+ devices. Sardine has raised ~$170M from Andreessen Horowitz, Visa, Experian, Google Ventures, FIS, and others. Public docs cover the risk landscape and integration overview; full API reference, SDKs, and sandbox access are gated and require a Sardine account.

providers.name: Briefcase
providers.description: Briefcase is an AI-native accounting and bookkeeping automation platform for UK accounting firms and businesses. Founded in 2024 in London by Reuben Steenkamp and Ján Stehlík, and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital, Entrepreneur First and Tiny, Briefcase describes itself as building the world's first AI autopilot for accounting firms. The product uses multimodal AI and agentic workflows to automate the most tedious parts of accounting: extracting data from invoices, receipts and bank statements, categorising transactions against a firm's chart of accounts, handling VAT (with embedded HMRC legislation for standard, reverse-charge and zero-rated VAT), automating prepayments and expense claims, and driving month-end and financial close. It publishes results into Xero and QuickBooks. Briefcase is delivered as a cloud SaaS application (app.briefcase.so); it is a consumer of accounting APIs rather than a public API producer, and at the time of this profile it publishes no developer/API documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs.

providers.name: Kivra
providers.description: Kivra provides a digital mailbox service for individuals and businesses in Sweden, allowing users to receive, store, and manage electronic mail, invoices, and official documents securely. The platform aims to reduce paper usage and streamline communication between citizens, companies, and public authorities, offering features such as digital receipts, payment handling, and identity verification through Kivra ID.

providers.name: Kyash
providers.description: Kyash Inc. (株式会社Kyash) is a Tokyo-based fintech founded in 2015 that operates a consumer mobile wallet and Visa prepaid card in Japan, covering charging, peer-to-peer transfers, shared accounts, buy-now-pay-later, personal finance management, and contactless payment through Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay. Kyash is a registered Funds Transfer Service Provider (Kanto Local Finance Bureau No. 00082) and a third-party Prepaid Payment Instrument Issuer (No. 00698), and is ISO/IEC 27001:2022, PCI DSS, and TRUSTe certified. Its business-facing product is Kyash Payout, a mass payout service that sends funds to Japanese domestic bank accounts or Kyash wallets at a flat 50 yen per transfer, integrated either by Zengin/CSV file upload or by direct API integration including a balance API. Kyash previously sold Kyash Direct, an API-based Visa card issuer processing platform launched in 2019. All API access is sales-gated: Kyash publishes no developer portal, API reference, specification, SDK, or sandbox.

providers.name: Talos
providers.description: Talos (Talos Global, Inc.) is the institutional platform to trade and manage digital assets across the full investment lifecycle. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in New York, NY, Talos unifies an order/execution management system (OEMS), a portfolio management system (PMS), and institutional market data on a single platform — covering price discovery, execution, portfolio construction, risk management, treasury, and settlement. Institutions such as hedge funds, banks, broker-dealers, asset managers, ETF issuers, and neobanks reach global liquidity through the Talos Network of 100+ providers (exchanges, OTC desks, prime brokers, custodians, DeFi protocols, and FX providers) and connect programmatically over FIX, REST, and WebSocket APIs. Developer documentation is gated behind client authentication (Auth0); this profile was enriched from Talos's public surface (llms.txt, GitHub org, and trust center).

providers.name: Askria
providers.description: Askria (askRIA) is an AI-powered due diligence and deal-management platform that provides decision infrastructure for private capital. It builds digital twins of investment funds and runs three AI agents: Discovery for thesis-matched company sourcing and outreach, Due Diligence for auto-scoring deals against custom frameworks while surfacing gaps and inconsistencies, and Portfolio for post-investment metric tracking and performance monitoring. The platform generates Investor Readiness Scores and streamlines the funding lifecycle for both investors and founders under a usage-based pricing model. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Leap Finance
providers.description: Leap Finance Inc. is a Bengaluru- and US-incorporated fintech that underwrites collateral-free education loans for Indian students pursuing graduate study abroad, underwriting on future earning potential and academic profile rather than family assets or collateral. The company originates and services study-abroad student loans covering tuition, living costs and travel, and also maintains www.leapscholar.com, its study-abroad counselling and IELTS preparation property. Leap Finance operates as a direct-to-consumer lender: it publishes a consumer web application, a partner portal and an Auth0-backed identity tenant, but does not operate a public developer program, publish API documentation, or ship a machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Lendbuzz
providers.description: Lendbuzz is a Boston-headquartered auto finance platform, founded in 2015, that uses machine learning and alternative data — bank transaction history, education, employment and income signals rather than a traditional FICO file — to underwrite consumers with thin or no US credit history. The company originates retail auto loans through a nationwide network of franchise and independent dealerships, and also provides dealers with floor planning and an AI-assisted "Express Contract" digital contracting flow. Dealers submit and manage deals through the Lendbuzz Dealer Portal at app.lendbuzz.com, or by routing credit applications through the Dealertrack and RouteOne F&I networks; consumers use a separate Client Portal. Lendbuzz Funding, LLC is a licensed lender (NMLS ID #1636296) and funds originations through recurring asset-backed securitizations. As of this profiling pass Lendbuzz publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract — partner integration is intermediated by Dealertrack and RouteOne.

providers.name: Vishwa
providers.description: Vishwa AI is an AI underwriting platform for credit teams, enabling screening, diligence, underwriting, and monitoring of deals across private credit, commercial real estate, private equity, and institutional lending. The platform extracts data, verifies with experts, and provides a 100% audit trail, tying every output back to source documents for comprehensive compliance and risk analytics.

providers.name: Brite Payments
providers.description: Brite Payments is a European payment institution offering instant, secure, and free-to-use online payments by connecting directly to thousands of banks across Europe. It enables merchants to accept “Pay by Bank” payments, providing instant checkout, refunds, and payouts without requiring card details. Brite serves both personal and business customers, supporting e‑commerce, charities, travel, utilities, and gaming, and emphasizes strong security, regulatory compliance, and a seamless user experience.

providers.name: M1 Finance
providers.description: M1 Finance is an automated investing platform offering fractional share portfolio management, smart money movement, margin borrowing, and integrated banking and credit features. The platform combines self-directed and automated investing through its Pies system, commission-free trading, a portfolio line of credit (M1 Borrow), high-yield cash accounts (M1 Earn), and a rewards credit card. M1 uses a GraphQL API gateway internally across 17+ microservices built on Scala and TypeScript to power its Finance Super App experience.

providers.name: Symmetrical
providers.description: Symmetrical.ai is a Polish-British HR and payroll fintech, founded in 2019 in Warsaw with offices in London and Barcelona and backed by Partech. It provides payroll and HR bureau outsourcing plus an HR platform automating wage calculation, digital document management, onboarding, leave and time tracking, and real-time analytics, alongside employee financial wellbeing tools such as earned-wage / salary-on-demand access. Symmetrical is ISO/IEC 27001 certified. The company operates an authentication-gated developer documentation portal (developer.symmetrical.ai) but publishes no public OpenAPI, API reference, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity plus probed security posture.

providers.name: Clutch
providers.description: Clutch (withclutch.com) is a US fintech that builds digital origination and lending automation software exclusively for credit unions. The platform spans consumer loan origination, deposit and business account opening, an omnichannel banker workstation (Fulfillment), an automated decisioning engine (Fastlane), targeted remarketing, data insights, and AI assistants — HAL for lending and Emma for collections — packaged as the Clutch Lending Automation System (LAS). Clutch integrates with credit union cores, loan origination systems such as MeridianLink Consumer LOS (LoansPQ), digital banking platforms and decisioning vendors, and reports powering origination for roughly 150 credit unions including six of the ten largest in the United States. Its customer-facing data surface is a File Transfer API and SFTP delivery for daily CSV exports covering lending, account opening, funding, NACHA and HAL conversation datasets; the API reference itself sits behind the customer support login.

providers.name: Nexi
providers.description: Nexi is a European payment technology company offering a wide range of digital payment solutions for merchants, banks, and consumers. It provides services such as card issuing, open banking, e‑commerce payments, and blockchain‑based solutions, operating across multiple countries in Europe. Nexi focuses on innovation in the PayTech sector, delivering secure, scalable, and compliant payment infrastructures for businesses of all sizes.

providers.name: Behavox
providers.description: Behavox is an AI-native compliance and conduct-surveillance software company serving the world's leading financial institutions and regulated enterprises. Its Unified AI Controls Platform spans directive, preventive, detective, and corrective controls — including Quantum (voice and text communication surveillance across 50+ languages and 150+ channels), Polaris (trade surveillance), Falcon (insider-threat and human-risk detection), Compass (conflicts of interest and personal account dealing), Atlas (control-room enforcement), Pathfinder (regulatory-change-to-policy), Intelligent Archive, Digital Employees, and Mosaic front-office revenue intelligence. Behavox is backed by Index Ventures and the SoftBank Vision Fund. The company sells directly to enterprise financial-services customers and does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Higlobe
providers.description: Higlobe is a regulated cross-border money transfer service that lets freelancers, independent contractors, and businesses receive international payments from clients in the United States and the European Union. Members open a USD or EUR receiving account, share a payment request or account details with their payer, and withdraw funds to a local bank account with near-instant, 24/7 settlement at a flat, low cost. The platform also offers a Visa Signature card, a yield on account balances, and payer-facing payment requests. Higlobe is registered as a Money Service Business (MSB) with FinCEN under the U.S. Department of the Treasury and publishes a SOC 2 Type 2 / SOC 3 security posture. Higlobe is a consumer/business fintech product and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity, security, and commercial surface. Backed by Battery Ventures; added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Linkable Networks (Collinson Group)
providers.description: Linkable Networks, Inc. is a Boston-based card-linked-offers (CLO) and SKU-linked-offers platform that lets consumers attach digital offers directly to the credit and debit cards already in their wallet. When a linked card is used for a qualifying purchase on the Visa, MasterCard, American Express or PayPal rails, the Linkable platform receives the transaction, optionally confirms item-level detail through the on-premises Linkable SKU Matcher, and delivers the savings back to the cardholder as a statement credit, eGift, points or miles - with no POS integration, no additional hardware or software, no punch cards and no employee training. The company sells to brands and retailers (product/SKU-level promotions funded with trade and co-op dollars), to loyalty program operators (single-purchase, multi-visit and aggregate-spend reward mechanics layered on an existing program), and to publishers and app developers, who integrate the consumer-facing MyLinkables REST API to display offers, link them to a cardholder, register consumers, manage linked payment accounts and track redemption. Linkable Networks is associated with the Collinson Group, the privately-owned global travel, loyalty and insurance operator behind Priority Pass, and was surfaced through the Bain Capital Ventures portfolio.

providers.name: Truss
providers.description: Truss provides banking services tailored for the construction industry, offering no monthly or account fees, fast payment processing for subcontractors and vendors, and expense management tools. Their platform enables construction businesses to get paid quickly via ACH and card payments, pay subs and vendors instantly, and manage finances without hidden costs, aiming to streamline financial operations in the building sector.

providers.name: Perpay
providers.description: Perpay is a buy-now-pay-later and credit-building platform that lets consumers shop and pay via automatic payroll deductions. Its internal REST platform supports marketplace checkout, installment plan creation, payroll direct-deposit switching (via Pinwheel), identity and income verification, and credit-bureau reporting to Experian, TransUnion, and Equifax. Perpay operates a closed marketplace — third-party merchant checkout integration is not publicly available; API access is reserved for Perpay's own products and vetted partners.

providers.name: Rabbet
providers.description: Rabbet (Renovate Simply, Inc.) is an Austin-based construction finance software company backed by QED Investors. It provides two products: a platform for real estate developers to manage construction budgets, draw packaging, and project documents, and a platform for construction lenders to standardize borrower submissions and manage construction loans with compliance controls. Rabbet operates a Public API (tracked on its status page) exposed through custom-scoped enterprise integrations that sync loan, funding, and project data with core banking systems (Fiserv, Finastra, FIS, Jack Henry), loan origination systems (nCino, MeridianLink, Encompass), and BI/data-warehouse tools (Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Amazon). API access is arranged through a scoping engagement rather than a self-service developer portal.

providers.name: Aforza
providers.description: Aforza is a cloud‑based fintech platform that helps enterprises and startups integrate financial services, payments, analytics, and route‑to‑market solutions through a unified set of APIs. The company offers secure, scalable, developer‑friendly endpoints for transaction processing, account management, reporting, and a suite of AI‑driven tools such as Ava. Backed by Bonfire Ventures, Aforza provides extensive documentation, SDKs, and support to accelerate product development and improve profitability across retail, distribution, and B2B commerce.

providers.name: Contadeo
providers.description: Contadeo provides electronic invoicing solutions authorized by the Ecuadorian SRI, offering free plans up to 10 invoices per month and paid tiers for higher volume. The platform enables rapid invoice generation, compliance with the latest 2026 regulations, and integrates with accounting tools. It targets small to medium businesses in Ecuador seeking streamlined, cloud‑based billing without credit‑card requirements.

providers.name: AdvisorCheck
providers.description: AdvisorCheck is a consumer-first platform for researching, comparing and continuously monitoring US financial advisors and the firms they work for. It compiles verified public regulatory data — FINRA BrokerCheck, the SEC's Investment Adviser Public Disclosure (IAPD) system, court records and six industry certification bodies — into profiles covering roughly 380,000 investment adviser representatives and 620,000 registered representatives. A free tier covers search and basic advisor monitoring; the paid AdvisorCheck Premium membership adds Advanced Monitoring with firm-stability insights (AUM changes, advisor headcount and retention, client acquisition trends, leadership and ownership changes, new firm disclosures). AdvisorCheck was founded in 2019, is headquartered in Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey with an office in Los Angeles, and raised a $1.8M seed round in June 2023. The company operates an application API at api.advisorcheck.com but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Billease
providers.description: Billease is a Philippine fintech company offering buy‑now‑pay‑later (BNPL) services and personal loans through its mobile app. Founded in 1969 as a rural bank, it now provides installment financing for online shopping, bill payments, and cash loans, targeting over 10 million users. The platform features zero‑interest credit lines, QR‑code payments, and integrates with thousands of merchants across the Philippines, regulated by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.

providers.name: Zoe Financial
providers.description: Zoe Financial is a New York based wealth management technology company operating a two-sided platform: Advisor Match, a concierge and algorithmic service connecting individuals with vetted independent fiduciary financial advisors, and the Zoe Wealth Platform, an all-in-one TAMP for registered investment advisers covering digital account opening, funding and ACAT transfers, sub-advisory trade execution, household-level automated rebalancing, tax-loss harvesting, a model marketplace, high-yield cash accounts, private labeling and outsourced middle-office operations. Zoe Financial, Inc. is an SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD 285158) and affiliate Zoe Securities LLC is a FINRA and SIPC member broker-dealer (CRD 326979), custodying through Apex Clearing and Charles Schwab. Zoe consumes partner APIs (BridgeFT, Salesforce, eMoney) but publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of its own.

providers.name: Ecton
providers.description: Ecton, Inc. is an AI-powered patient payments platform focused on reducing the financial stress and financial toxicity that surround healthcare costs. Its flagship product, Toni, is an AI financial counselor that gives patients personalized guidance on medical bills, insurance, and payment options, paired with a Health Savings and Spending Wallet for managing and paying healthcare expenses. Ecton helps healthcare providers strengthen patient relationships, improve treatment adherence, and increase revenue collection. The company is HIPAA-aligned and backed by General Catalyst. Ecton does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and public security posture.

providers.name: Finary
providers.description: Finary is a French fintech platform for personal wealth tracking and management that aggregates a user's entire net worth — stocks, funds, ETFs, cryptocurrency, real estate, savings, life insurance, startups and other alternative assets — into a single dashboard by connecting to 20,000+ banks and brokers worldwide. Beyond tracking, Finary offers fee detection, diversification and sector/geo allocation analysis, dividend monitoring, budgeting, in-app crypto buying/selling and staking, and life-insurance products. The company reports more than one million users and is regulated in France by the AMF and ACPR. Finary does not publish an official public REST API or SDKs; the app frontends talk to a private API that the developer community has reverse-engineered into an unofficial OpenAPI spec and language wrappers.

providers.name: TravelBank
providers.description: TravelBank, a U.S. Bank company, is an all-in-one corporate travel, expense, and card management platform used by more than 45,000 companies. It combines travel booking for flights, hotels, and cars with expense tracking, corporate and virtual card reconciliation, approval workflows, and reporting, and ships pre-built integrations with QuickBooks, NetSuite, Xero, U.S. Bank, and Brex. TravelBank publishes no public developer API: its platform API at api.travelbank.com is private and undocumented, and integrations are pre-built or delivered as custom work.

providers.name: Comulate
providers.description: Comulate is an accounting automation and revenue intelligence platform built for large insurance brokers. It captures carrier statement data across spreadsheets, PDFs, and email, then automatically reconciles direct-bill and carrier-payables transactions against policies to eliminate manual back-office accounting work. Its Revenue Intelligence layer adds commission forecasting, variance tracking, and missing-commission detection. Comulate is delivered as a hosted application at app.comulate.com with native connectors to broker management systems including Epic, BenefitPoint, AMS360, Microsoft Dynamics, and Salesforce. The company was surfaced as a Bond Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API or documentation as of this profile.

providers.name: SentiLink
providers.description: SentiLink is an identity fraud prevention platform that empowers financial institutions to transact confidently by stopping synthetic identity fraud, account takeover, and first-party fraud at the point of account application and beyond. The platform provides a REST API delivering real-time scores and signals derived from behavioral and identity data, enabling lenders, banks, credit unions, and fintechs to make instant, accurate decisions without adding friction to the onboarding experience.

providers.name: Trustdock
providers.description: TRUSTDOCK Inc. (株式会社TRUSTDOCK) is a Tokyo-based digital identity and eKYC (electronic Know Your Customer) provider founded in November 2017. The company delivers high-precision, fast, and low-cost online identity verification and digital ID infrastructure via API, serving more than 300 enterprise and government clients across finance, insurance, ride-sharing and car-sharing, telecommunications (MNO/MVNO), real-estate crowdfunding, second-hand/reuse goods, recruitment, matching apps, and public-sector onboarding. TRUSTDOCK offers both browser-based and mobile-app-based verification flows, holds ISMS (ISO 27001) certification and the Japanese PrivacyMark, and participates in the OpenID Foundation Japan KYC Working Group and the FIDO Alliance. Its API documentation is provided to customers under NDA rather than published to a public developer portal.

providers.name: Cardless
providers.description: Cardless, Inc. is a San Francisco fintech that operates an embedded co-branded credit card platform, letting consumer brands launch and run their own credit card programs natively inside their own apps and websites. The platform pairs a partner API surface with pre-built components covering the full credit journey — application and identity verification, real-time decisioning, checkout with instant virtual cards, card management and transaction disputes — while Cardless handles issuing-bank relationships, card production, underwriting, fraud, KYC/AML compliance, servicing and support behind the scenes. It is network-agnostic across Visa, Mastercard and American Express. Named partners include Coinbase (Coinbase One Card), Bilt, Qatar Airways Privilege Club, Alibaba.com, LATAM Airlines, Avianca LifeMiles, TAP Air Portugal and Avelo Airlines. Developer documentation at docs.cardless.com is gated behind a partner login, so no public OpenAPI, SDKs or sandbox credentials are published.

providers.name: Firstbase
providers.description: Firstbase is an all-in-one startup operating system that helps founders form, run, and grow a US business from anywhere in the world. Its products cover incorporation (Firstbase Start for LLCs and C-Corps in Delaware, Wyoming, New York, Texas and more), ongoing compliance and registered-agent services (Firstbase Agent), bookkeeping, invoicing and tax-ready financials (Firstbase Accounting), tax filing, and a virtual business address (Firstbase Mailroom). Firstbase markets an embedded "Incorporation API" for platforms that want to offer company formation to their own users, but publishes no public developer documentation, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve developer portal for it. Firstbase is a venture-backed company (a16z portfolio) added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: Wealthsimple
providers.description: Wealthsimple is a Toronto-based Canadian financial technology company, founded in 2014, offering a full suite of consumer financial products: managed investing (Invest), self-directed stock and ETF trading (Trade), cryptocurrency, tax filing (Tax), spending, saving, and cash and card products. It serves more than four million Canadians with roughly CAD $125 billion in assets under administration and reached a CAD $10 billion valuation in its 2025 Series F round. Wealthsimple does not publish an official public developer API or OpenAPI specification; programmatic account access is available only through open-banking aggregators (SnapTrade, Plaid) and community-built unofficial libraries. This profile captures the company's public trust, security, and developer-adjacent surface (security.txt, HackerOne bug bounty, Trust Center, status page, verified GitHub organization).

providers.name: Xapo
providers.description: Xapo Bank is a members-only private bank and Bitcoin custodian founded in 2013, combining regulated fiat banking with institutional-grade Bitcoin custody in a single app. Members earn interest on Bitcoin and USD balances, borrow against Bitcoin without selling, invest in US stocks and ETFs, and transact globally in multiple currencies. Xapo Bank Limited is regulated by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission as a credit institution (Permission No. 23171), with Xapo VASP Limited licensed as a DLT Provider (Permission No. 26061). The company publishes SOC 2 Type II / SOC 3, PCI DSS, and GDPR compliance claims but operates app-only today, with no public developer API or portal; legacy Xapo Bitcoin API SDKs remain on PyPI and RubyGems from its pre-bank wallet era.

providers.name: ABN AMRO
providers.description: A Dutch banking and financial services group serving retail, private, and corporate clients across Europe. ABN AMRO publishes a public developer portal exposing PSD2 Open Banking, Tikkie payment-request, and corporate payment APIs.

providers.name: Amber Group
providers.description: Amber Group is a global digital asset financial services firm founded in 2017 by former traditional-finance traders, providing trading, liquidity provision, wealth and asset management, staking, and treasury solutions for institutions and high-net-worth clients. Its institutional platform, Amber Premium (Nasdaq: AMBR), operates from financial hubs including Singapore, Hong Kong, and Dubai, and publishes the Amber Premium Global API service suite so clients can integrate trading, liquidity, and account services into their own systems. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures, Pantera Capital, and Paradigm and enriched with the company's public developer, legal, and support surfaces.

providers.name: Candex
providers.description: Candex is a fintech "master vendor" platform that lets large enterprises engage, track, and pay long-tail, one-time, and hard-to-onboard suppliers across more than 50 countries without setting each vendor up in their own ERP or finance systems. A buyer configures Candex once; when it needs to purchase from a small or irregular supplier, it transacts with Candex, which handles supplier onboarding, tax and banking validation, compliance scans, PO and non-PO invoicing, and cross-border payment execution, then remits to the actual supplier. By consolidating tail-spend vendors and their records, Candex reduces administrative overhead, increases spend visibility and control, and makes "No PO, No Pay" policies achievable. The company integrates with existing procurement and finance stacks via API and bulk upload, but publishes no public developer portal or API reference.

providers.name: Finicom
providers.description: Finicom offers a platform that synchronizes bank transaction data with applications such as Google Sheets, Notion, Airtable, Zapier, and Slack. It supports connections to over 12,000 financial institutions in the US and Canada and provides features like AI‑powered receipt and statement imports, real‑time notifications, and team collaboration tools. The service is available for personal use at no cost and includes paid tiers for additional connected banks and destinations.

providers.name: FlexPoint
providers.description: FlexPoint is an AI-native billing and accounts receivable (AR) platform built specifically for managed service providers (MSPs). It automates the invoice-to-cash lifecycle across five jobs: Sync (pull billing data from PSA and accounting systems), Send (issue invoices), Collect (chase and recover overdue invoices), Process (card and ACH payments including Same-Day ACH and AutoPay), and Reconcile (match deposits to the general ledger via GL Connect). FlexPoint's AR Agents autonomously send payment reminders, follow up on overdue invoices, and surface collection priorities. The platform integrates with the accounting, ERP, PSA, quoting, and automation tools MSPs already run (QuickBooks, Xero, Sage Intacct, NetSuite, Business Central, ConnectWise, HaloPSA, Autotask, SuperOps, Quoter, QuoteWerks, Rewst, DataGate) and offers API access for custom integrations. FlexPoint is backed by Foundry Group and Techstars.

providers.name: IRALOGIX
providers.description: IRALOGIX is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania fintech that operates a cloud-native, white-label IRA (Individual Retirement Account) recordkeeping and administration platform for financial institutions — banks, wealth managers, brokerages, recordkeepers and advisors — who use it to offer digital IRA programs under their own brand. The platform covers onboarding, contributions, trading, distributions, rollovers, compliance monitoring and administration end to end, and the company markets "API-driven connectivity and real-time data flows" that integrate with existing custodial and recordkeeping infrastructure rather than replacing it. The developer surface is partner-gated: documentation at docs.iralogix.com sits behind Okta visitor authentication and the partner console at partner.iralogix.com behind an Auth0 tenant, so no public OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or SDK is published. The company states SSAE SOC 2 Type 1 and SSAE SOC 1 Type 2 attestation.

providers.name: Pipe
providers.description: Pipe is an embedded financial OS that lets platforms — vertical SaaS, payment facilitators, and marketplaces — offer capital and cash-flow tools to the small and medium-sized businesses on their platform without those businesses ever leaving it. Its marquee product, Capital, delivers pre-approved funding offers priced from a business's transaction data, with repayment tied to sales performance rather than fixed monthly payments. Partners integrate via prebuilt embedded UI components, a zero-code Pipe-hosted flow, or a customizable REST API, while Pipe handles the banking partnerships and compliance. Backed by Anthemis and Creandum. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Pipe's public pages; the full API reference lives behind password-gated partner docs at docs.pipe.com.

providers.name: Swedbank Pay
providers.description: Swedbank Pay provides a comprehensive, end‑to‑end payment platform for merchants and developers across Sweden and the Nordics. It offers in‑store, online, and acquiring solutions, along with a developer portal, sandbox environment, and extensive documentation to integrate payments, recurring billing, and tokenisation into web, mobile, and POS applications.

providers.name: Duitku
providers.description: Duitku provides a payment gateway platform in Indonesia, enabling merchants to accept online payments via various methods such as credit cards, bank transfers, e‑wallets, and QR codes. It offers APIs for payment processing, disbursements, and transaction management, with features like real‑time monitoring, fraud protection, and multi‑currency support. The service is tailored for the Indonesian market, emphasizing ease of integration and comprehensive documentation for developers.
